  VERNON CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING

  PUBLIC COMMENT

  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  1.  City of Vernon Vacancies and Recruitment and Retention Efforts
  Recommendation: A. Conduct a Public Hearing; and B. Receive and file an
  informational report and presentation on the City of Vernon vacancies, and
  recruitment and retention efforts pursuant to Assembly Bill 2561/Government Code
  Section 3502.3.

  Human Resources Director Tan presented the staff report and Human Resources
  Manager Grizelle conducted a PowerPoint presentation.

  Mayor Ybarra opened the public hearing at 9:09 a.m. There being no speakers,
  Mayor Ybarra closed the public hearing at 9:10 a.m.

  Mayor Ybarra invited further Council discussion. There being none, Mayor Ybarra
  called for a motion.

  MOTION
  Council Member Larios moved and Council Member Merlo seconded a motion to
  approve recommendations A and B. The question was called and the motion
  carried unanimously.

  CONSENT CALENDAR

  Mayor Ybarra invited public comments. There being none, Mayor Ybarra, called
  for a motion.

  MOTION
  Mayor Pro Tem Rivera moved and Council Member Rodriguez seconded a motion
  to approve the Consent Calendar. The question was called and the motion carried
  unanimously

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:
  2.  Meeting Minutes
  Recommendation: Approve the May 19, 2026 Regular City Council Meeting
  Minutes.
  3.  Operating Account Warrant Register
  Recommendation: Approve Operating Account Warrant Register No. 174, for the
  period of April 19, 2026 through May 2, 2026, totaling $8,583,363.87 and
  consisting of ratification of electronic payments totaling $8,373,680.98 and
  ratification of the issuance of early checks totaling $209,682.89.

  4.  Public Works Department Monthly Report
  Recommendation: Receive and file the April 2026 Building Report.
  5.  Report on Contract Award to Invoice Cloud Approved by the City
  Administrator
  Recommendation: Receive and file the report on the award of Amendment No. 1
  to the Contract with Invoice Cloud for processing of online payments and donations
  as approved by the City Administrator pursuant to Vernon Municipal Code Sections
  3.32.110(B)(2) and 3.32.110(B)(3).
  6.  Annual Statement of Investment Policy for Fiscal Year 2026-2027
  Recommendation: Adopt Resolution No. 2026-023 approving an Annual Statement
  of Investment Policy for Fiscal Year 2026-27 and delegating investment authority
  to the Director of Finance/City Treasurer.
  7.  Contract with DASH Construction Company Inc. for Citywide Street Tree
  Planting Project
  Recommendation: A. Find that award of the proposed contract is categorically
  exempt under the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) in accordance with
  CEQA Guidelines Section 15304, because the Project consists of only minor
  alterations in the condition of land, water and/or vegetation that does not involve
  removal of healthy , mature, scenic trees is merely to repair existing streets and
  involves no expansion of existing use; B. Accept the bid proposal from DASH
  Construction Company, Inc. as the lowest responsive and responsible bidder, and
  reject all other bids; C. Approve and authorize the City Administrator to execute a
  contract with DASH Construction Company, Inc. in substantially the same form as
  submitted, in an amount not-to-exceed $484,900; and D. Authorize a contingency
  amount of ten percent (10%) or $48,490 in the event of an unexpected changed
  condition in the Project, and grant authority to the City Administrator to issue
  change orders for an amount up to the contingency amount, if necessary.

  NEW BUSINESS
  8.  Brown Act Updates Related to Senate Bill 707
  Recommendation: A. Receive a presentation on Brown Act updates related to the
  teleconferencing and accessibility provisions under Senate Bill 707 (SB 707); B.
  Adopt Resolution No. 2026-024 Approving a Technology Disruption Policy; and C.
  Adopt Resolution No. 2026-025 Determining “reasonable efforts” for outreach to
  encourage participation in City Council meetings.

  City Clerk Rocha presented the staff report.
  Mayor Ybarra invited public comments and there were none.
  Mayor Ybarra inquired about the steps the City had taken to implement and test
  the two-way communication system. City Clerk Rocha explained that the remote
  participation option was used during the COVID-19 pandemic and periodically had
  been utilized with outside consultants who participated in the meeting remotely.

  Additionally, it had recently been utilized at the Business and Industry Commission
  meeting.
  Mayor Ybarra called for a motion.
  MOTION
  Council Member Larios moved and Council Member Rodriguez seconded a motion
  to approve recommendations A, B, and C. The question was called and the motion
  carried unanimously.
  9.  Amendment to Classification and Compensation Plan
  Recommendation: A. Approve revised job descriptions and reclassifications; and
  B. Adopt Resolution No. 2026-026 adopting the Classification and Compensation
  Plan in accordance with Government Code Section 20636(b)(1) and repealing
  Resolution No. 2026-004, effective February 17, 2026.

  Human Resources Director Tan presented the staff report.

  Mayor Ybarra invited public comments. There being none, Mayor Ybarra called for
  a motion.

  MOTION
  Mayor Pro Tem Rivera moved and Council Member Merlo seconded a motion to
  approve recommendations A and B. The question was called and the motion
  carried unanimously.

  10.  Franchise Towing Service Agreement
  Recommendation: A. Introduce and conduct the first reading of Ordinance No.
  1313 granting Mr. C’s Towing of South Gate, Inc., a franchise towing services
  agreement for a term of three years; and B. Direct staff to schedule the second
  reading and adoption of Ordinance No. 1313 for the June 16, 2026, City Council
  meeting.

  Police Chief Sousa presented the staff report.

  Discussion ensued and Council Member Larios requested that Chief Sousa
  explain the Request for Proposals (RFP) process, and Chief Sousa explained the
  selection process.

  Council Member Larios inquired about whether there was anything that set Mr. C's
  apart from other companies and the reasoning behind moving from three to a
  single provider. Chief Sousa commented on Mr. C's proven track record and noted
  their strong partnership with the department. He mentioned that their fees were
  typically at or below average, and their response time was excellent compared to
  other top providers. Additionally, they could accommodate heavy loads, and they
  had a tow yard next door in Maywood, which made it convenient for staff and
 Docusign Envelope ID: D00B0739-F494-8CA9-8014-585DD145F418

  Regular City Council Meeting Minutes  Page 5 of 9
  June 2, 2026

  residents. Regarding the decision to move to a single operator, Chief Sousa
  explained that staff found that, with the other two tow providers, the companies did
  not fully staff the required services, and their response times were slower, whereas
  Mr. C’s has consistently met the 30-minute response time.

  City Attorney Moussa-Milward clarified that the contract with Mr. C’s was not an
  exclusive franchise agreement. Per the City’s Municipal Code, selected or non-
  winning bids can be placed on a list to be used by the City.

  Council Member Merlo expressed concern about comments she came across
  about the service provided by Mr. C’s in neighboring cities and wanted to ensure
  the City was acting ethically.

  Mayor Ybarra asked whether the franchise fees collected by the City cover the
  City’s administrative costs, and Chief Sousa confirmed that they did.

  Mayor Ybarra called for public comment. There being none, Mayor Ybarra called
  for a motion.

  City Clerk Rocha read the title of Ordinance No. 1313 into the record.

  Council Member Larios requested that staff provide updates to the City Council
  regarding Mr. C’s services and inform the City Council of any complaints received.

  MOTION
  Mayor Pro Tem Rivera moved and Council Member Rodriguez seconded a motion
  to approve recommendations A and B. The question was called and the motion
  carried unanimously.

  11.  2026 Military Equipment Use Policy Ordinance and Report
  Recommendation: A. Review and approve the 2026 Military Equipment Report;
  and B. Renew Ordinance No. 1282, approving the Police Department’s military
  equipment funding, acquisition, and use policy.

  Police Chief Sousa presented the staff report.

  Mayor Ybarra invited public comments. There being none, Mayor Ybarra called for
  a motion.

  MOTION
  Council Member Larios moved and Council Member Merlo seconded a motion to
  approve recommendations A and B. The question was called and the motion
  carried unanimously.

  12.  Fiscal Year 2026-27 Budget Workshop II
  Recommendation: Conduct a workshop and provide direction to staff on the Fiscal
  Year (FY) 2026-27 estimated revenues and proposed expenditures in preparation
  for FY 2026-27 Citywide Budget adoption.

  City Administrator Saeki presented the staff report.
  City Administrator Saeki provided an overview of the Strategic Plan Expenditures,
  which were one-time expenditures, and introduced Vernon City Elementary School
  Principal Leonora Carrillo, who presented a request to the City Council to fund the
  School Interventionist position. The position was previously funded through a
  grant, but in the upcoming fiscal year, the school budget cannot sustain it.

  School Interventionist Maria Nercessian also provided information about the
  interventionist program and its positive impact on students.

  City Administrator Saeki requested direction from the City Council on whether they
  wanted to continue with the one-time expenditures for the Strategic Plan Initiatives,
  which he estimated totaled approximately $540,000.

  Mayor Ybarra inquired what the City was doing to reduce expenses and avoid
  burdening businesses, given that the City was considering an electricity rate
  increase in addition to other taxes businesses already pay. City Administrator
  Saeki responded that the City had taken steps to present a balanced budget; the
  total number of full-time employees had not increased; staff positions were frozen
  or underfilled; and staff had been reduced where possible without cutting projects.

  Mayor Ybarra opined that perhaps some projects could be delayed; she
  recognized the need for the for the 4% increase in electric rates; however, rising
  costs were impacting everyone.

  There was discussion amongst the City Council regarding potential cuts, funding
  the requested position for Vernon City Elementary School, providing relief to the
  local businesses, and funding the one-time expenditures for the Strategic
  Initiatives.

  Mayor Pro Tem Rivera and Council Member Larios both stated they agreed to fund
  the Interventionist position for Vernon City Elementary.

  There was a consensus from the City Council to defer the Library Nook,
  which was estimated at $38,000.

  Mayor Ybarra stated she was not in agreement to fund the school’s request.
  Council Member Larios noted the importance of funding the school’s request.
 Docusign Envelope ID: D00B0739-F494-8CA9-8014-585DD145F418

  The City Council asked Principal Carrillo additional questions regarding the
  student-teacher ratio, the percentage of students assessed and served specifically
  by the Interventionist, and the school’s plan if funding for the position were not
  received. Principal Carrillo stated that 1/3 of their students receive the services.
  She also explained the impact of losing the position: tutoring would still be
  provided, but fewer students would be served.

  Council Member Larios inquired whether the City could afford to absorb a
  $200,000 position. Mayor Ybarra asked what the actual cost of the School
  Interventionist position was, and Principal Carrillo stated it was approximately
  $180,000, not including future labor negotiations.

  Council Member Rodriguez asked what the plan was for the following year if the
  position is not funded by the School District. Principal Carrillo stated the School
  District was working on a plan.

  City Administrator Saeki stated that the proposed budget could absorb the cost of
  funding the position because there is a $240,000 surplus, and if the City Council
  was not comfortable with doing so, they could consider a $3 million surplus from
  the last fiscal year and allocate it as a one-time expenditure.

  Mayor Ybarra asked whether the surplus could be transferred to Vernon Public
  Utilities to help with the deficit, and City Administrator Saeki stated that it would be
  a policy decision the City Council would need to make; there could be potential
  legal issues, it is not a common practice, and staff would need to research further
  before responding to the question.

  Mayor Ybarra stated that she preferred to defer the budget decision until that
  question could be answered.

  Council Member Larios stated she would prefer to provide the requested direction
  to staff.

  MOTION
  Mayor Pro-Tem Rivera moved, and Council Member Larios seconded a motion to
  approve the Interventionist position for Vernon City Elementary. The question was
  called, and the motion carried 4-1 with Mayor Ybarra voting in opposition.

  Finance Director Hui presented an overview of the general budget.

  Public Utilities General Manager, Todd Dussenberry, and Assistant Public Utilities
  General Manager Richard Corbi, presented an overview of the proposed electric
  rate increase and staff’s recommendation to simplify the utility bill for customers by
  combining the Energy Cost Adjustment (ECA) and Renewable Portfolio Standard
  (RPS) rates to have a base rate that will cover expenses and have one charge for
  the services provided.
 Docusign Envelope ID: D00B0739-F494-8CA9-8014-585DD145F418

  Regular City Council Meeting Minutes  Page 8 of 9
  June 2, 2026

  Mayor Ybarra asked what the Business and Industry Commission's
  recommendation was. Public Utilities Manager Dusenberry informed the City
  Council that the sentiment of the Commission was to increase the utility rates by
  4% for the fiscal year 2026-27, study the increase for the following year and
  evaluate over the course of the year whether the increase was needed; set the
  ECA at 1 cent and the RPS at 1 cent, and keep the ECA and RPS fees separate
  on the billing statement.

  Mayor Ybarra invited public comments.

  Cathy Browne, General Manager at Crown Poly, spoke on the impact of increased
  utility costs on their business operations in Vernon. She stated the company now
  faces financial challenges due to rising costs, including demands for an 8% utility
  charge. Browne expressed concern over the company's inability to hire, the need
  to cut incentives, and plans to halt expansion in Vernon. She urged the council to
  consider tough budget choices to support local businesses.

  Marisa Olguin of the Vernon Chamber stated that the general fund currently stood
  at $52 million, a significant recovery from a previous deficit. Olguin recalled a
  decision made in 2018-2019 to outsource fire services to manage a $19.26 million
  budget due to rising retirement costs. She raised concerns regarding the Police
  Department’s funding, which exceeded 50%. Olguin noted that an urgent
  evaluation was needed to ensure the city maintains its safety and budget integrity.

  Public Utilities General Manager Dusenberry stated he understood the business
  community’s concerns. He emphasized the City’s commitment to customer care.
  He acknowledged the challenges faced by the utility and highlighted a goal of
  improving service and rates in the upcoming years. Despite past difficulties, he
  was optimistic about the progress the city would make over the next three to five
  years, aiming for significant improvements while maintaining cost savings.

  Mayor Ybarra recommended accepting the Business and Industry Commission's
  recommendation to keep the 4% utility rate, maintain the ECA at one cent, and
  reduce the RPS from 1.5 cents to one cent. The City Council expressed agreement
  with this approach, leading to a motion and a second from Council members to
  move forward.

  MOTION
  Mayor Ybarra moved and Council Member Larios second a motion to direct staff
  to implement the Business and Industry Commission’s recommendation regarding
  the utility rates, which was to increase the utility rates by 4% for the fiscal year
  2026-27, set the ECA at 1 cent and the RPS at 1 cent, and keep the ECA and RPS
  fees separate on the billing statement. The question was called and the motion
  carried unanimously.
